article.articleHeadline: बारिश के साथ बढ़ा बीमारियों का खतरा! मुंबई में डेंगू-स्वाइन फ्लू के मामले तेजी से बढ़े
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Increased risk of diseases with the rains! Dengue and swine flu cases rise rapidly in Mumbai.
article.articleSummary: Mumbai faces increased risk of dengue, leptospirosis, and swine flu amid ongoing monsoon rains and urban flooding. Heavy rainfall across the city has caused waterlogging, creating breeding conditions for mosquitoes and exposure to contaminated mud, elevating dengue and leptospirosis risks. Last July's figures showed dengue rising by about 58% and leptospirosis by about 79% there, signaling a similar danger this monsoon season. Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) has intensified vector control, including fogging around more than 3 million homes and extensive insecticide campaigns. Health officials urge residents who have walked through pooled water or mud to seek medical advice within 24 to 72 hours and not to ignore fever during monsoon; prompt doctor consultation is advised. The article underscores protective measures and early diagnosis to curb outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: 雨とともに病気のリスクが増加!ムンバイでデング熱・豚インフルエンザの症例が急増
triage.triage_reason: ムンバイでモンスーン期に季節性の感染症（デング熱、レプトスピラ症、豚インフルエンザ）が例年通り増加している事象であり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは低いが、当局が対策を強化しており経過観察が妥当。
triage.notes: モンスーン期の季節性感染症の増加であり、前年比の数値上昇はあるが例年の傾向内。BMCによる媒介動物対策強化が報告されており、国レベルでの管理は可能と見られる。

article.articleHeadline: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية وسط جهود مكثفة لاحتوائه
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo amid intensified efforts to contain it.
article.articleSummary: As of July 15, 2026, Ebola re-emerges in the Ituri region of eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with numerous deaths among affected families. Health teams have imposed strict containment measures, including restricting families from approaching the deceased to curb transmission. Doctors face difficulties, especially with Ebola infections among medical staff, which heightens containment challenges. Authorities report the outbreak is widening and say response efforts have been intensified, calling on residents to cooperate more fully with surveillance and control measures to halt further spread.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が発生、封じ込めに向けた対策強化
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCイトゥリ州で再発し、複数の死者と医療従事者への感染が報告されており、拡大傾向にあるためIHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 医療従事者への感染が報告されており、院内感染拡大のリスクが高い。続報でのケース数・致死率・国際対応状況の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola Fight in DRC Needs Urgent Action, Faster Response
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo remains uncontrolled, spreading to five provinces—Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, Haut-Uélé and Tshopo—with 2,111 confirmed cases and 750 deaths reported as of July 13. Ongoing conflict, insecurity, displacement and limited access complicate response efforts. UNICEF outlines four priorities: mobilizing communities and countering misinformation, strengthening infection prevention and control, protecting affected children, and expanding community-based surveillance. Progress includes nurseries near Ebola centers that provide safe spaces for children when parents are hospitalized, contributing to psychosocial recovery for a three-month-old and hope for a nine-month-old. The response must be integrated with other emergencies—malnutrition, cholera, polio, forced displacement—while maintaining essential health services and preparing for the next school year. With only about 25% of required funding available, urgent resource mobilization and sustained international solidarity are essential to contain the epidemic.

triage.headline_ja: DRCにおけるエボラ対策には緊急かつ迅速な対応が必要
triage.triage_reason: DRCで5州に拡大した制御不能なエボラ流行（確定2,111例、死亡750例）が継続しており、資金不足・治安悪化により国際支援が急務であるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する重大シグナルと判断。
triage.notes: コレラ・ポリオも同時流行として言及されているが、記事の主題はエボラ流行であり、DRC国内の複数州（イトゥリ、南キブ、ツショポ等）にまたがる大規模アウトブレイクとして継続的なモニタリングが必要。資金確保率が25%と低く、国際社会の支援強化が急務とされている点も重要。

article.articleHeadline: الكونغو تسجل أكثر من 2000 إصابة بإيبولا وسط مخاوف من تفشٍ أوسع
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Democratic Republic of the Congo reports more than 2,000 Ebola cases amid fears of a wider outbreak.
article.articleSummary: 2,011 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 754 deaths reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of July 15, 2026, in what authorities describe as the fastest-spreading outbreak, extending to five provinces. About 753 patients remain in isolation or in hospital, with 366 recoveries. The World Health Organization cautions the true scale may be two to four times higher, noting 80% of new infections arise from transmission chains not traced to known contacts and many fatalities occurring in communities without healthcare access. Médecins Sans Frontières says the pace is unprecedented, with cases tripling in under five weeks and deaths more than quintupled. The outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo Ebola strain, for which no licensed vaccine or treatment exists. A first clinical trial for a potential drug, “Ebo-Pep,” has begun, evaluating the antiviral remdesivir from Gilead. Separately, health workers at Bunia General Hospital protested delayed pay, with a similar strike at a Romabara treatment center in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ感染2,000人超を報告 さらなる拡大への懸念
triage.triage_reason: 致死率の高いエボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）が5州に拡大し、症例が急速に増加、ワクチン・治療薬未承認かつ追跡不能な感染連鎖が80%を占めるため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当。
triage.notes: WHOは実際の症例数が公式報告の2〜4倍に上る可能性を指摘。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo株による前例のない拡大速度で、国際的な支援と監視が急務。医療従事者のストライキも対応能力に影響を及ぼす可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: تفشي إيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية وسط جهود مكثفة لاحتوائه
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo amid intensive efforts to contain it.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-15, Ebola outbreak persists in Ituri province, eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, with casualties reported among affected families. Health teams are enforcing stringent containment measures, including restricting families from approaching the bodies of the deceased to prevent transmission. Medical personnel are facing significant challenges, as infections among frontline staff complicate containment efforts. Authorities have intensified response activities and are urging residents to cooperate with surveillance and control measures as the outbreak widens. The report underscores ongoing containment work, protection of healthcare workers, and prevention of secondary spread within communities in Ituri. No specific case counts or laboratory confirmation details are provided; the focus remains on burial restrictions, rapid case finding, and community engagement to halt transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱が発生、封じ込めに向けた集中的な取り組みが進行中
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱はIHR基準に該当する重大疾患であり、医療従事者への感染拡大や地域拡大の兆候があるためフルRRAが必要。
triage.notes: 具体的な症例数や検査確定情報は記載されておらず、医療従事者感染や地域拡大の詳細は続報待ち。

article.articleHeadline: Supermercado em Paraty tem estoque interditado após fiscalização encontrar micos, pombos e fezes de roedores - Diário do Rio de Janeiro
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Supermarket in Paraty has its stock embargoed after an inspection found monkeys, pigeons and rodent droppings - Rio de Janeiro Daily
article.articleSummary: Paraty, Rio de Janeiro, Brazil: A supermarket stockroom was embargoed after inspectors found monkeys, pigeons, rodent droppings, and rodent poison in contact with foods. The joint operation by Sedcon, Procon-RJ, Paraty Procon, and the Military Police identified pest-control failures, poor hygiene, and improper storage. The stock will remain closed until all irregularities are corrected, including pest-control services, thorough cleaning, structural adjustments to block animal entry, and environmentally compliant removal of the animals. Authorities emphasized leptospirosis risk linked to rodent contamination in the region. In a separate inspection at another Paraty market, a dead spider was found on displayed foods. In total, over 154 kilograms of items deemed unfit for consumption were discarded, including kibbeh flour, sour cassava starch, and sweetened condensed milk. Both stores were fined and given 15 days to present administrative defenses.

triage.headline_ja: パラチのスーパーマーケット、検査でサル・ハト・ネズミの糞が見つかり在庫が差し押さえに - リオデジャネイロ・デイリー
triage.triage_reason: 食品衛生違反に関する行政指導の記事であり、実際のレプトスピラ症患者発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す情報はない。
triage.notes: 記事はスーパーの衛生違反による行政処分が主題で、レプトスピラ症のリスクに言及しているのみで実際の感染症発生事例ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Curitiba vai ganhar reforço no combate à dengue; entenda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Curitiba will receive reinforcements in the fight against dengue; here's what that means.
article.articleSummary: Curitiba, Brazil, will bolster its dengue fight by releasing Wolbachia-infected Aedes aegypti mosquitoes in the Sítio Cercado neighborhood starting July 29, 2026, for 26 weeks. The Wolbachia bacteria reduce transmission of dengue, Zika, and chikungunya by blocking virus replication in the mosquito. The project, a collaboration with Wolbito do Brasil, follows successful implementations in Foz do Iguaçu (Paraná) and Niterói (Rio de Janeiro), where dengue cases declined—up to 89% in Niterói. Curitiba's effort targets areas with higher mosquito-foci incidence; officials deliver household guidance and stress continued personal dengue-control measures. The program uses both adult mosquitoes and eggs released into the environment. Success will depend on community engagement and ongoing vector-control practices alongside the releases.

triage.headline_ja: クリチバ、デング熱対策を強化へ；その内容を解説
triage.triage_reason: 既存のデング対策プログラム（ウォルバキア感染蚊の放出）の拡大に関する予防的取り組みの紹介記事であり、新規の異常な公衆衛生事象や急増を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事はデング熱・ジカ熱・チクングニア熱の媒介蚊対策（ウォルバキア技術の導入拡大）に関するもので、症例急増や異常な流行を報じるものではない。他地域（フォス・ド・イグアス、ニテロイ）での過去の成功事例が言及されているが、いずれもブラジル国内。

article.articleHeadline: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo top 2,000, with 754 dead
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-15, the Democratic Republic of the Congo reports 2,011 confirmed Ebola cases and 754 deaths amid an outbreak centered in Ituri province, which borders Uganda and South Sudan. Across five provinces, 753 patients are currently being treated in hospitals or isolation centers. Uganda has also recorded Ebola cases, including two deaths. South Kivu has reported no new cases for 47 days. Ebola is a life-threatening viral disease transmitted by direct contact with infected people and their bodily fluids. The Bundibugyo strain drives the current outbreak; there is no specific vaccine or targeted treatment yet. Clinical trials of two antiviral therapies have been underway since early July.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ確定症例が2,000件を超え、死者754人に
triage.triage_reason: DRCで2,011例・754人死亡の大規模エボラ流行が継続し、ウガンダへも拡大しているためIHR基準に複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダでも死亡例が報告されているが対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。致死率が高く（約37%）、ワクチン・特効薬未確立のため国際支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: Ministério da Saúde recebe contribuições do mercado para desenvolver encomenda tecnológica que identificará tuberculose
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health receives market input to develop a technology procurement that will identify tuberculosis.
article.articleSummary: On July 8, 2026, Brazil's Ministry of Health opened a public consultation for a Technology Purchase (ETEC) to develop a portable, low-cost tuberculosis detector that requires no complex lab infrastructure and can identify resistance to rifampicin and isoniazid. Supported by the Brazilian Industrial Development Agency (ABDI) under a Technical Cooperation Agreement (ACT), the effort will map technical and economic requirements to guide a future bid to build the device. Eligible Brazilian entities must be national-based, registered, and active in the last 12 months; consortia with public institutions or foreign firms may participate. Submissions via a virtual form are due by Aug 8; a final report will be published in August to shape the procurement edital and contracting later this year. Individual meetings may be requested by July 17; virtual sessions run until July 31 and will be recorded.

triage.headline_ja: 保健省、結核を特定する技術調達開発のため市場からの意見を募集
triage.triage_reason: これは結核診断技術の政策的な公開調達手続きに関する記事であり、実際の感染症発生や公衆衛生上の緊急事態を報告するものではない。
triage.notes: 本記事はブラジル保健省による結核検出装置開発のための技術調達（ETEC）に関する公開協議の告知であり、疾病発生状況の報告ではないため、シグナルトリアージの対象外と判断した。

article.articleHeadline: DR Kongo: Ebola breitet sich ungewöhnlich rasant aus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo: Ebola is spreading unusually rapidly.
article.articleSummary: DR Congo experiences an unusually rapid Ebola outbreak. By mid-July 2026, authorities report more than 2,000 cases and 754 deaths across five provinces since the outbreak was declared on May 15. WHO notes this is the fastest-spreading Ebola epidemic to date; official counts may underestimate true numbers by two- to fourfold. About 80% of new cases are not linked to known contacts, suggesting transmission through unidentified routes and many deaths occurring outside medical facilities. Burial practices and fear hinder containment. In July, residents in Ituri's Bafwabango burned an Ebola treatment center after protests; a police officer was killed and patients fled. Response includes about 800 beds in treatment centers and 14 laboratories; $115 million pledged for six months, only 40% received. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo variant with no approved vaccine or therapy; a Gilead antiviral Obeldesivir is in clinical trials.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国:エボラ出血熱が異例の速さで拡大
triage.triage_reason: WHOが史上最速の感染拡大と評価するエボラ出血熱の大規模アウトブレイクであり、死者754名、感染経路不明の症例が8割を占めるなど公衆衛生上深刻かつ国際的関心が高い事案。
triage.notes: WHOはこのアウトブレイクを史上最速拡大のエボラ流行と評価。ワクチン・治療薬未承認のBundibugyo株が原因で、資金不足（必要額の40%のみ確保）と地域住民による治療施設焼き討ちなど封じ込め上の重大な障害が発生している。

article.articleHeadline: Kangra to conduct study on TB burden, disease hotspots - The Tribune
article.articleSummary: 14 TB-related deaths in Q2 2026 in Kangra district per the District TB Death Audit under NTEP, with deaths mainly linked to advanced co-morbidities and non-TB causes. Deputy Commissioner Hemraj Bairwa directs strengthening critical care and a district-wide study to map TB burden, hotspots, and vulnerable groups to accelerate elimination. Referral centers at Civil Hospitals Nurpur, Palampur, Dehra; Zonal Hospital Dharamsala; and Dr Rajendra Prasad Government Medical College, Tanda, will handle critically ill TB cases. Emphasis on early diagnosis, prompt hospitalization, and integrated management of diabetes, hypertension, chronic respiratory diseases, and malignancies; intensive home-based follow-up and regular monitoring; expanded palliative care. Programs include TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan 2.0, Universal Drug Susceptibility Testing, TB preventive treatment, Nikshay Mitra, community screening, and Ayushman Aarogya Shivirs for integrated TB/NCD screening.

triage.headline_ja: カングラ地区、結核の疾病負担とホットスポットに関する調査を実施へ
triage.triage_reason: 既存の結核対策プログラムの一環としての通常業務であり、異常な増加や新規性はなく、公衆衛生上の緊急性も認められない。
triage.notes: 結核は既知の風土病であり、本記事は地方自治体による通常の疾病負担調査・対策強化に関する内容。死亡例も併存疾患が主因とされている。

article.articleHeadline: Médicos Sin Fronteras: ébola avanza a ritmo sin precedentes
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Doctors Without Borders: Ebola advances at an unprecedented pace.
article.articleSummary: As of 15 July 2026, MSF reports the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is expanding at an unprecedented pace and into new areas. In under five weeks, confirmed cases have tripled and deaths quintupled, with the government listing 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 fatalities. Declared on 15 May in Ituri province (northeast, mineral-rich and under armed groups), this is the 17th Ebola outbreak in the DRC and the third-largest and fastest-growing on record, with spread into neighboring Uganda and additional zones. The World Health Organization notes Bundibugyo-variant infections could be two to four times higher than official estimates. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected humans or animals, causing fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and severe hemorrhagic fever. MSF calls for urgent, coordinated international action to reinforce the medical response.

triage.headline_ja: 国境なき医師団:エボラ出血熱、前例のない速さで拡大
triage.triage_reason: DRCで確認例が5週間で3倍、死者が5倍に急増し、ウガンダにも拡大するエボラ出血熱アウトブレイクであり、IHR基準の複数該当と国際的関心の高さからフルRRAへの移行が妥当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en Ituri : les résultats d'un Institut supérieur uniquement à la radio(Secrétaire général académique) - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Ituri: the findings of a higher education institute aired exclusively on radio (Academic Secretary-General) - ACP.
article.articleSummary: Bunia, Ituri, Democratic Republic of the Congo — On 15 July 2026, the Institut supérieur pédagogique (ISP) de Bunia announced the 2025-2026 academic results via Radio Candip and online to support Ebola virus disease (EVD) prevention. The results proclamation, after deliberations that day, will be broadcast at 18:30 local time and accessible worldwide at www.rtccandipispbia.net. The ceremony will involve the jury presidents for Literature & Humanities and for the Exact Sciences, alongside the management committee, broadcasting from the Radio Candip studio. This remote format breaks with the institution’s traditional public on-campus proclamation, aiming to minimize physical contact and reinforce Ebola prevention measures in Ituri as part of the ongoing response.

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo: Hospital Municipal de Americana reforça importância da prevenção e diagnóstico precoce das hepatites virais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July: Americana Municipal Hospital reinforces the importance of prevention and early diagnosis of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: Viral hepatitis A, B, and C are key concerns, with Americana Municipal Hospital in Americana highlighting prevention and early diagnosis during July Yellow. Hepatitis A is linked to contaminated water and food; hepatitis B and C are transmitted through blood and sharps, unprotected sex, and, in some cases, mother-to-child transmission. Infections are often asymptomatic early; when present, signs include fatigue, nausea, abdominal pain, dark urine, pale stools, and jaundice. Prevention emphasizes safe hygiene, not sharing blood-contact tools, condom use, and choosing facilities with proper biosafety for procedures like tattoos or piercings. Vaccination against A and B is promoted: hepatitis B vaccine for newborns and unvaccinated adults; pentavalent at 2, 4, and 6 months (includes Hep B); hepatitis A vaccine at 15 months and for special groups. The SAE in Americana offers rapid Hep B and C testing (Mon–Fri, 9:00–15:00), about 450 tests monthly, with active case finding and ministry-certified quality.

triage.headline_ja: イエロー・ジュライ：アメリカーナ市立病院がウイルス性肝炎の予防と早期診断の重要性を強調

article.articleHeadline: Gilead begins Ebola antiviral trial as cases approach 2,000 in Democratic Republic of Congo
article.articleSummary: On 15 July 2026, Gilead began testing the antiviral oberdesivir as post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) in the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The EBO-PEP trial aims to enroll about 1,000 participants who had direct exposure to a confirmed case within the past five days and are asymptomatic; participants (adults or 12 years+) are monitored daily for 21 days, with a final visit on day 42. The outbreak now shows 1,984 Ebola infections and 721 deaths overall, with Ituri reporting 1,772 confirmed cases. Of total cases, 37 new cases and 17 deaths were reported; all but 21 cases and two deaths have occurred in the DRC, while one case is in France and 20 cases with two deaths are in Uganda. A successful EBO-PEP could formalize PEP as a breakthrough Ebola prevention method, alongside contact tracing and community engagement, per WHO Director-General Tedros.

triage.triage_reason: DRCで約2,000症例・721死亡の大規模エボラ流行が継続し、既にウガンダ・フランスへ国際的に拡大しているため、IHR基準の複数該当が明確。

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo: Jaru promove ação de prevenção às hepatites virais em Tarilândia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July: Jaru promotes a viral hepatitis prevention action in Tarilândia.
article.articleSummary: July Yellow campaign action in Tarilândia district of Jaru, Rondônia, Brazil, focusing on viral hepatitis prevention, early diagnosis, and treatment. On Tuesday, July 21, from 7:30 to 11:30, at Izaltino de Andrade Lopes Health Unit, the Municipal Health Secretariat (Semusa), in partnership with the Specialized Care Service (SAE), will offer prevention guidance and education on HIV self-test usage. An external outreach will distribute prevention kits at local shops and in other community spaces. Kits contain HIV self-test, male and female condoms, and informational materials on preventing viral hepatitis and sexually transmitted infections. The initiative aims to expand access to prevention resources and strengthen linkage to public health services, emphasizing early diagnosis. The national Julho Amarelo campaign seeks to raise awareness of viral hepatitis risks, which are preventable, diagnosable, and treatable when detected early.

article.articleHeadline: Vacinação Contra O Sarampo Em São Bernardo é Intensificada Com 'dose Zero' Para Bebês Após Casos Suspeitos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles Vaccination in São Bernardo Intensified with 'Dose Zero' for Babies After Suspected Cases.
article.articleSummary: As of 15 July 2026, São Bernardo do Campo, Brazil, intensified measles vaccination with a 'dose zero' for all children aged 6 months through 11 months 29 days amid four suspected local cases. Dose zero is available at 35 Basic Health Units; the routine schedule remains two doses at 12 and 15 months, with adults up to 29 years advised to have two doses, 30–59 years one dose, and health professionals two doses. Immunization director Jessica de Cássia Santos Soares highlighted high local coverage, noting the city is the region's only area to meet the BCG Target, with coordinated efforts across primary care, education, and community health workers. Two of the four suspected cases could be import-related. On 9 July, two blocking sweeps near the first cases’ residences visited over 520 homes, interviewed more than 800 people, and administered 89 vaccine doses; most residents were up to date.

article.articleHeadline: Health workers' strike hampers Congo's Ebola fight; confirmed cases cross 2,000-mark
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (Ituri province, Bunia) since May 15 has surpassed 2,000 confirmed cases. Two months into the outbreak, transmission outpaces tracking; about 80% of new infections arise from unknown transmission chains. Contact tracing coverage of exposed contacts stands at 67%, and authorities have yet to identify patient zero. Displacements from armed conflict and mining movements hinder tracing of thousands who had contact with infected individuals. Many recent deaths occur in communities without health facility care. Health workers across Ituri are on strike, with reports of non-payment since outbreak onset. There are no approved vaccines or treatments for Bundibugyo virus, unlike Zaire Ebola, complicating response. A study enrolling in Ituri probes two potential Ebola therapies.

triage.headline_ja: 医療従事者のストライキがコンゴのエボラ対策を妨害、確認症例数が2,000人を突破
triage.triage_reason: エボラ(Bundibugyoウイルス)の大規模アウトブレイクで確認症例が2000人を超え、80%が未知の感染経路、承認済みワクチン・治療法がなく、医療従事者のストライキも発生しており、国際的拡大・公衆衛生上の深刻な影響が懸念される。
triage.notes: Bundibugyoウイルスによるエボラ出血熱で、Zaireウイルスとは異なり承認済みワクチン・治療法が存在しない点が特に懸念される。武装勢力による住民移動や医療従事者のストライキが対応を困難にしている。

article.articleHeadline: Parasite provoquant la diarrhée | Les autorités fédérales ne s'inquiètent pas de l'importation d'aliments
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Diarrhea-causing parasite | Federal authorities are not concerned about food imports.
article.articleSummary: As of July 15, 2026, cyclosporiasis outbreaks tied to fresh produce in the United States have prompted no import restrictions by Canada's CFIA. Since May, US CDC reports about 7,000 infections across several states; more than 1,600 cases confirmed and roughly 5,100 under investigation. Michigan has the majority, with lettuce/leafy greens suspected; no single producer tied to the outbreak. Canada's Public Health Agency states Cyclospora is not transmitted person-to-person and is not typically present in Canadian drinking water. CFIA surveillance targets leafy greens (whole or cut), prepackaged salads, herbs (cilantro, basil), raspberries and blackberries, and is intensified during higher-risk seasons. Preventive measures include import controls when needed, and thorough washing; cooking produce from regions with Cyclospora (Peru, Mexico, India, Nepal, Guatemala, Southeast Asia, Dominican Republic) may reduce risk.

triage.headline_ja: 下痢を引き起こす寄生虫 | 連邦当局は食品輸入について懸念していない
triage.triage_reason: 米国・カナダでのサイクロスポーラ症アウトブレイクであり、対象国（India等）は感染リスク地域として言及されているに過ぎず、実際の発生国ではない。人-人感染がなく、カナダは輸入制限を行っていないため懸念は低い。
triage.notes: 記事の主題は米国（ミシガン州中心）とカナダの対応であり、インド・ネパール・ペルー等はCyclospora常在地域として一般的に言及されているのみで、当該国での発生事例ではないため対象国リストから除外した。

article.articleHeadline: US says its citizens in DRC must spend 21 days elsewhere before return to prevent Ebola spread
article.articleSummary: On July 15, 2026, the United States announced a Do Not Board order for American citizens who have traveled to the Democratic Republic of Congo to prevent the spread of Ebola. The directive bars affected travelers from boarding commercial flights to the United States unless the individual spends 21 days elsewhere before attempting return. This public health measure targets travel-related Ebola risk linked to the DRC and aims to limit importation of the virus via air travel. The article does not specify case counts, symptoms, laboratory confirmations, or enforcement details beyond the 21-day requirement. It represents a containment strategy focused on imported/exported risk and underscores ongoing concerns about Ebola transmission tied to the DRC.

triage.notes: 記事はDRCにおけるエボラ流行を背景とした米国の渡航管理措置に関する内容であり、症例数・感染規模等の詳細情報は記載なし。DRCでの具体的な流行状況については別途確認が必要。米国(6252001)は対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。

article.articleHeadline: Minsa realiza videoconferencia internacional: Estrategias Integrales para el Control del Dengue Frente al Cambio Climático y El Niño
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health Holds an International Videoconference: Comprehensive Strategies for Dengue Control in the Face of Climate Change and El Niño.
article.articleSummary: Peru's Ministry of Health (MINSA) will host a free videoconference, 'Comprehensive Strategies for Dengue Control in the Face of Climate Change and El Niño,' led by the National School of Public Health (ENSAP) to strengthen health professionals nationwide. The session analyzes Dengue trends in Peru amid El Niño and climate change, evaluates vector prevention and control strategies, and reviews diagnostic testing and the laboratory network during higher transmission. It addresses early detection, clinical management, and case follow-up amid rising health-service demand due to climate events, and outlines challenges from El Niño and Emerging and Epidemic Diseases. Notable speakers include Amy C. Morrison, PhD (University of California); Ana Cecilia Ribeiro (Evandro Chagas Institute, FIOCRUZ, Brazil); César Munayco Escate, Director of Peru’s National Center for Epidemiology, Prevention and Control of Diseases; Yuri Alegre Palomino, Director of Metaxenic and Zoonotic Diseases; and Bessy Lescano Cabellos, infectious disease physician at ENSAP.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : les équipes de riposte contre Ebola reprennent leurs activités après des assurances du gouverneur militaire - LePotentiel
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: Ebola response teams resume their activities after assurances from the military governor.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease response teams in Ituri resume activity on July 15, 2026, in Bunia and Rwampara health zones after assurances from military governor General-major Gaby Kasongo Mulumba that remuneration delays would be regularized. A consultative meeting with field providers and the Ebola response Strategic Coordination, led by Professor Pierre Akilimali (Incident Manager), addressed delays due to irregular beneficiary lists and a verification phase before fund disbursement to ensure data reliability. The governor pledged to accelerate validation and payments, restoring dialogue. Consequently, providers suspended protests and immediately resumed Ebola response operations. Field teams are carrying out patient care, epidemiological surveillance, prevention activities, and community sensitization. Continued interventions are deemed essential to curb Ebola spread in Ituri, while administrative and financial regularization discussions proceed.

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo: 4 mitos e verdades sobre a transmissão das hepatites virais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July: 4 myths and truths about the transmission of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: During Yellow July in Brazil, awareness emphasizes prevention and early diagnosis of viral hepatitis. From 2000-2024, Brazil registered over 826,000 confirmed viral hepatitis cases, with hepatitis C accounting for 41.5% and hepatitis B for 36.6%. Mortality has declined thanks to vaccination and improved testing/treatment, but infections often progress silently. Transmission is primarily via contact with contaminated blood. Four myths are addressed: (1) Tattoos can transmit hepatitis if needles or materials aren’t disposable or properly sterilized; regulated studios reduce risk. (2) Sharing nail clippers or razor blades poses risk even without visible blood. (3) All hepatitis show symptoms early—false; many infections remain asymptomatic for years. (4) Manicure instruments can transmit hepatitis; sterilization between clients or using individual tools is crucial. Public health messages underscore biosafety and routine screening for those at risk.

article.articleHeadline: 新冠病毒感染大幅上升 大陸中青年猝死頻發
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 infections surge sharply; sudden deaths among middle-aged and young people in mainland China are frequent.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 infections surge in mainland China in June 2026, with 79,000 new confirmed cases—roughly 70% of January–May total and 2.4 times June 2025. SARS-CoV-2 positivity in sentinel influenza-like-illness surveillance rose from 2.9% to 6.4% by late June; the national data report 130 severe cases and 1 COVID-19–related death (with underlying conditions). Hong Kong and Macao also report rising COVID-19 activity. In parallel, a wave of sudden deaths among middle-aged and younger Chinese professionals is noted: Sun Fanglin, 58, president of Tongji University Translational Medicine Institute, died July 10, 2026; other recently reported deaths include Liao Ke, 37, independent director of Red Star Securities; Sun Benhua, 54, Northwest A&F University professor; Gao Shanwen, 55, economist; Du Daming, 59, Beijing Institute of Technology professor. Officials warn public data may underrepresent true extent.

triage.triage_reason: 中国本土でCOVID-19感染者数が前年比2.4倍に急増し、香港・マカオでも活動上昇が報告されている。中壮年層の突然死増加への社会的関心も高く、続報監視が必要。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: COVID-19 infections surge; sudden deaths among middle-aged and younger people in Mainland China are occurring frequently.
article.articleSummary: June 2026 saw a surge of COVID-19 infections in Mainland China, with 79,000 new confirmed cases—about 72% of the Jan–May total (109,000) and 2.4 times June 2025. Severe cases numbered 130; one death was reported in June with comorbidity. Sentinel surveillance showed SARS-CoV-2 positivity among influenza-like illness visits rising from 2.9% in early June to 6.4% late June. Amid the surge, reports describe sudden deaths among middle‑aged and younger professionals: Tongji University professor Sun Fanglin, 58, died July 10; Liao Ke, 37, independent director of Red Tower Securities; Sun Benhua, 54, Northwest A&F University professor; Gao Shanwen, 55, former chief economist of Guotou Securities; and Du Daming, 59, Beijing Institute of Technology professor. At least eight mid-career academics and executives died in June, including Xue Yan Hua, 37, Suzhou University. Hong Kong and Macao also show rising infections and deaths; official data are viewed skeptically.

article.articleHeadline: 刚果民主共和国埃博拉确诊病例超过2000例
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Over 2,000 confirmed Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of July 15, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues to surge, with more than 2,000 laboratory-confirmed cases. Since the outbreak began in May, 754 people have died and 366 have recovered. The rapid spread marks an historic acceleration, with the WHO warning that continuing transmission could trigger broader regional effects. Médecins Sans Frontières calls for an urgent intensification of response efforts, including expanding testing, patient care, survivor support, and safe burial practices, to quickly detect and isolate new cases. The World Health Organization notes roughly 750 isolation and treatment beds across 25 healthcare facilities in the DRC, with a further 100 beds to be added this week. International partners, including the U.S. CDC, are coordinating with local and global health actors to bolster contact tracing, specimen collection, and community outreach.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国、エボラ確診症例が2000例を超える
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで2000例を超え、致死率も高く急速に拡大しており、WHOが地域的波及への警戒を表明していることからIHR基準・WPRO基準の複数に該当する。
triage.notes: WHO、MSF、米CDCなど複数の国際機関が対応を強化しており、フルリスク評価が必要な事案。

article.articleHeadline: أكثر من 2000 إصابة بإيبولا في الكونغو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: More than 2,000 Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of July 16, 2026, Ebola virus disease caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus has infected over 2,000 people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with at least 754 deaths. The outbreak has spread to five provinces, including Ituri in the northeast, and the World Health Organization cautions the true scale may be 2–4 times the official count. There is currently no licensed vaccine or treatment for this Bundibugyo strain. A first clinical trial of a potential drug, EBO-PEP, began on Tuesday to evaluate remdesivir’s effectiveness in confirmed cases. MSF warns the outbreak is expanding into new areas at an unprecedented pace; in less than five weeks, confirmed cases have tripled and deaths more than quintupled. The current outbreak already surpasses half of the cases from the 2018–2020 outbreak in the DRC, with 80% of new cases not linked to known contacts, indicating unknown transmission chains and late care seeking.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ感染者2,000人超
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱（ブンディブギョ株）がDRC5州に拡大し、2,000人超の感染・754人以上の死亡、ワクチン・治療法未確立、80%が感染経路不明という重大かつ異常な公衆衛生事象であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 承認済みワクチン・治療薬が存在しないブンディブギョ株による大規模流行。WHOは公式数値の2〜4倍の実際の規模を懸念しており、MSFも前例のない拡大速度を警告。フルリスク評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Ebola di Kongo Menyebar Lebih Cepat dari Perkiraan
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Outbreak in Kongo Spreading Faster Than Expected
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading faster than containment efforts, MSF warns as confirmed cases exceed 2,000. The latest figures show 2,011 laboratory-confirmed cases and 754 deaths, a case fatality rate of 37.5% since the outbreak was declared on May 15. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus has affected five provinces—Haut-Uele, Ituri, Nord-Kivu, Sud-Kivu, and Tshopo—and 41 health zones; WHO reports 42 health zones affected in the past week. MSF notes transmission is expanding to new areas at unprecedented speed, with many new cases from undetected chains of transmission. Africa CDC has launched first clinical trials in DRC and Uganda evaluating post-exposure prophylaxis with obeldesivir for Ebola. MSF calls for increased resources, community engagement, surveillance, testing, dignified burials, and faster international action.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、予想より速いスピードで拡大
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で確認症例2,000人超・致死率37.5%のエボラ流行が5州41〜42保健地区に拡大し、封じ込めを上回る速度で感染が広がっているため、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められる。
triage.notes: ウガンダでの臨床試験実施が言及されているが、感染拡大自体はDRC国内に限定されており、ウガンダは対象国リストにも含まれないため verified_locations には含めていない。

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en Congo rebasa la respuesta sanitaria, alerta la OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in Congo outpaces the health response, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: As of 15 July 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, continues expanding faster than response capacity, with no approved treatment or vaccine. The epicenter is Ituri Province, with at least 1,926 suspected or confirmed cases and 702 deaths reported across three provinces; additional cases in neighboring Uganda. WHO emergency director Chikwe Ihekweazu notes most recent deaths occurred at home and 80% of new infections arise from unknown transmission chains, hampering containment. Response capacity has improved to about 800 beds and laboratories increased from 1 to 14 in Bunia, yet challenges persist: funding gaps, attacks on facilities, armed conflict in the east, and community distrust. A strike by staff at a treatment center in the northeast adds to disruption. Investigators have begun clinical trials to evaluate potential treatments in hopes of stabilizing the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ流行、医療対応能力を上回る速度で拡大とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRCで大規模拡大（症例1,926件、死者702人）し国境を越えてウガンダにも波及、承認された治療法・ワクチンがなく公衆衛生上深刻な影響とWHOも警鐘を鳴らしており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダへの症例拡大が報告されているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めていない。武力紛争・資金不足・医療施設への攻撃・スタッフのストライキなど対応を阻害する複合的要因が存在し、WHOによる緊急対応が続いている。

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo: 4 mitos e verdades sobre a transmissão das hepatites virais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July: 4 myths and truths about the transmission of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: During Yellow July, the awareness month for viral hepatitis, health professionals emphasize prevention and early diagnosis of viral hepatitis. Viral hepatitis is transmitted primarily through contact with contaminated blood and can affect the liver, ranging from mild disturbances to severe outcomes such as cirrhosis and liver cancer. Despite advances in vaccination, screening, and treatment, these infections remain a public health challenge because many cases progress silently. The article, aligned with the month’s campaign, discusses four myths and truths about transmission and highlights the ongoing need for vaccination, routine testing, and timely diagnosis to curb spread and disease progression. It underscores that prevention strategies—alongside improved access to care and surveillance—are crucial to reducing the burden of hepatitis worldwide. Published July 15, 2026, the piece frames viral hepatitis as preventable and manageable with continued public health effort.

triage.headline_ja: イエロージュライ：ウイルス性肝炎の感染に関する4つの神話と真実
triage.triage_reason: 啓発キャンペーンに関する一般的な健康情報記事であり、特定の異常事態や新規アウトブレイクの報告ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の感染症発生事例ではなく、啓発月間に関する一般的な予防啓発記事であるため、監視対象イベントには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola : baisse d'activités pour commerçants et tenanciers de bars, après deux mois d'épidémie - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Slump in Business Activity for Merchants and Bar Owners After Two Months of the Outbreak - ACP
article.articleSummary: Two months into an Ebola outbreak centered in Ituri, the city of Beni in North Kivu, Democratic Republic of Congo, merchants and bar owners report sharp declines in business. The Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak has prompted social distancing and venue closures, reducing customer turnout: shops report slowed clothing sales; a nearby terrace formerly crowded after 3 PM now seats only a few. Fish sellers saw revenue drop as cross-border trade with Uganda halts; prices per kilogram fall from six fish to four. Transportation costs have risen due to distancing: a Beni–Butembo ride (54 km) now costs about 30,000 FC instead of 20,000 FC (roughly a 35% increase), and travel from Goma to Beni costs about $80 instead of $50. The minister declared the 17th Ebola outbreak on May 15, with the epicenter in Ituri.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ:流行から2ヶ月、商人やバー経営者の営業活動が落ち込む - ACP
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で公式に宣言された第17次エボラ出血熱流行が2ヶ月継続しており、国境を越えた貿易停止や社会的距離確保策など深刻な社会経済的影響が生じているため、フルリスク評価が必要。
triage.notes: ウガンダとの国境貿易停止が言及されているが、ウガンダ国内での症例確認は記事に記載なし。イトゥリ州を震源とする第17次エボラ流行（ブンディブギョ株）で、保健大臣が5月15日に宣言済み。既知の進行中アウトブレイクだが経済的影響の拡大が新規性あり。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا في الكونغو: 2000 إصابة وتحذيرات من منظمة الصحة العالم
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in Congo: 2,000 cases and warnings from the World Health Organization
article.articleSummary: 2,000+ Ebola virus disease cases reported in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with 754 deaths, amid spread of the Bundibugyo lineage that currently has no licensed vaccine or approved treatment. WHO warns official counts may underestimate the outbreak by 2–4 times and notes spread across five provinces, prompting an urgent international response. A first clinical trial began last Tuesday to evaluate an experimental drug, Obildesivir, under WHO oversight. Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has issued a plea to intensify medical intervention, reporting transmission in new areas at an unprecedented pace; confirmed cases have tripled in under five weeks and deaths have quintupled. Current totals already exceed half of the cases recorded in the last major wave (2018–2020). Security conditions challenge frontline teams, adding pressure on healthcare systems.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱:2,000件の感染とWHOからの警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で2,000例以上・死亡754人のエボラ（ブンディブギョ株）流行が5州に拡大し、WHOが過小報告の可能性と国際的対応の必要性を警告しているため、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当。
triage.notes: 承認されたワクチン・治療法がないブンディブギョ株の流行で、症例数・死亡数が急増中。WHOは公式集計が実数の2〜4倍過小評価の可能性を指摘。治安状況が対応を困難にしている。フルRRAでの詳細評価が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Estados Unidos impone medida para sus ciudadanos provenientes de la República Democrática del Congo: deberán esperar 21 días en otro país por el ébola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: United States imposes a measure on its citizens arriving from the Democratic Republic of the Congo: they must wait 21 days in another country due to Ebola.
article.articleSummary: US citizens who have traveled to the Democratic Republic of the Congo are barred from boarding flights to the United States unless they have spent 21 days outside the DRC, as part of Ebola outbreak containment; non-citizens from the DRC were already prohibited. The DRC has reported over 2,000 Ebola cases and at least 754 deaths across five provinces, with the outbreak spreading into new areas at an unprecedented pace. MSF warns the number of confirmed cases has tripled and deaths quintupled in under five weeks, and notes the outbreak has surpassed half of the total cases from the 2018–2020 RDC epidemic. WHO says 80% of new cases are not in known contact lists and arise from unknown transmission chains, many from people who died before seeking care. The Bundibugyo variant dominates; estimated cases may be 2–4 times official counts. No vaccines or standard treatments exist yet, though the first antiviral trial began on Tuesday.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、コンゴ民主共和国からの帰国市民に対しエボラ出血熱対策として他国での21日間待機を義務付け
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で前例のない速さで拡大するエボラ出血熱（2000例超・死者754人以上）を受け、米国が渡航制限を課しており、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する重大シグナルである。
triage.notes: 米国は対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsから除外。感染は5州に拡大し、80%が既知の接触者リストに含まれない未知の感染経路から発生しているとWHOが報告。Bundibugyo株が優勢で、実際の症例数は公式発表の2〜4倍と推定される。ワクチン・標準治療薬はまだ存在せず、抗ウイルス薬の治験が開始されたばかり。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : plus de 2000 cas d'Ebola, MSF alerte
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: more than 2,000 Ebola cases, MSF warns.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continues to expand, with 2,011 laboratory-confirmed Ebola cases and 754 deaths since the May 15, 2026 declaration. Case fatality is 37.5%. The epidemic now spans Haut-Uele, Ituri, North Kivu, South Kivu, and Tshopo. MSF warns that the virus is moving into new health zones and that response resources are insufficient, with more infections and families losing loved ones. The WHO reports geographic expansion from 36 to 42 health zones in a week and cautions that true numbers may be higher due to unlinked transmission chains. MSF attributes the surge to Bundibugyo Ebola and calls for accelerated international mobilization, stronger surveillance, diagnostics, and safer corpse management. Africa CDC has launched a first clinical trial in DRC and Uganda for post-exposure prophylaxis with obeldesivir.

triage.headline_ja: DRC:エボラ症例2,000人超、MSFが警告
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国でエボラ出血熱の大規模流行が進行中で、症例数2,000人超・致死率37.5%と重篤かつ複数州へ地理的拡大しており、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はウガンダをAfrica CDCの治験実施国として言及しているが、実際の流行発生国はDRCのみであり、ウガンダでの症例発生は言及されていないため verified_locations から除外した。

article.articleHeadline: MS registra 1,5 mil casos confirmados de dengue e segue sem nenhuma morte pela doença
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ministry of Health reports 1,500 confirmed dengue cases and remains without any deaths from the disease.
article.articleSummary: As of 13 July 2026, Mato Grosso do Sul reports 1,548 confirmed dengue cases and 9,187 confirmed chikungunya cases. Dengue deaths remain zero to date, with more than 4,800 probable dengue cases and two deaths under investigation. Chikungunya shows 28 confirmed deaths with two more under investigation, and about 12,900 probable chikungunya cases under investigation. High dengue incidence is concentrated in Santa Rita do Pardo, Corumbá, Angélica, Batayporã, Selvíria, Costa Rica, Ladário, Amambai, Jardim, Paraíso das Águas, Douradina, Jaraguari, and Pedro Gomes; Campo Grande has low incidence. For chikungunya, 24 cities are in high-incidence areas, including Douradina, Paraíso das Águas, Angélica, Batayporã, Fátima do Sul, Sete Quedas, Dourados, Jardim, Corumbá, Dois Irmãos do Buriti, Guia Lopes da Laguna, Bonito, Amambai, Ladário, Aquidauana, Itaporã, Vicentina, Nioaque, Anastácio, Selvíria, Jateí, Água Clara, Sidrolândia, and Jaraguari. Bulletin released 13 July; ongoing public health surveillance and investigation continue.

triage.headline_ja: マット・グロッソ・ド・スル州、デング熱1,548例確認、死亡者ゼロ継続
triage.triage_reason: デング熱・チクングニア熱の症例数は多いが、ブラジルにおいて季節性・地域流行的な疾患であり異常性は低い。ただしチクングニア熱による28名の死亡例は注視が必要。
triage.notes: 州保健当局による定期的なサーベイランス報告。デング熱は死亡者なしだが、チクングニア熱は9,187例確認・28例死亡と重症度が高い。地域内での持続的な媒介蚊感染が懸念されるが、国際的拡大や渡航制限の情報はなし。

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo reforça prevenção e diagnóstico precoce das hepatites virais
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July reinforces prevention and early diagnosis of viral hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: Viral hepatitis awareness and early-diagnosis efforts in Catanduva, Brazil, are intensified throughout July under the Yellow July campaign. The Municipal Health Secretariat is rolling out activities led by the Testing and Counseling Center (CTA) on Rua Pará near the Medical Specialties Center (CEM), including training for health network staff, educational guidance, distribution of self-test kits, and expanded rapid testing for residents and professionals. Outreach will also occur at strategic sites, such as Praça da Matriz and the Rodoviário Bus Terminal, to explain transmission, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment. The campaign peaks on World Hepatitis Day (July 28), with a full-day mobilization at the CTA featuring rapid testing, counseling, educational materials, self-test distribution, and referrals for treatment when needed. Training sessions for health workers are scheduled for July 16, 23, and 30; rapid tests are free, with SUS providing follow-up care and treatment for confirmed cases.

triage.headline_ja: 「黄色い7月」キャンペーン、ウイルス性肝炎の予防と早期診断を強化
triage.triage_reason: アウトブレイクではなく、ブラジル自治体による毎年恒例の肝炎啓発・検査キャンペーンの告知であり、公衆衛生上の異常事態を示すものではない。
triage.notes: 記事は疾病アウトブレイクではなく、公衆衛生啓発キャンペーン（World Hepatitis Dayに関連）の告知。疾患名にContagious Equine Metritisが含まれているが本文とは無関係。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يتوغل في الكونغو الديمقراطية ويقتل المئات.. تفاصيل الفيروس الخطير - الوطن
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola spreads in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and kills hundreds... Details of the deadly virus - Al-Watan.
article.articleSummary: Across the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ebola virus disease has surpassed 2,000 cases and 754 deaths, with 753 patients under treatment or isolation and 366 recoveries since the outbreak began. Authorities call it the fastest-spreading Ebola outbreak in the country’s history, involving strains including Bundibugyo, with the ministry noting the outbreak began on May 15. Transmission occurs from infected animals such as fruit bats to humans, and human-to-human via blood or body fluids, contaminated objects, or handling of the deceased. Early symptoms resemble malaria and typhoid, complicating diagnosis. Prevention emphasizes avoiding contact with cases or animals, isolation, contact tracing, and strict hygiene in health facilities. The WHO recommends stronger surveillance, laboratory capacity, staff training, and rapid-response teams, while travel restrictions are not advised. Follow-up of contacts has not exceeded 67%.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で拡大し、数百人が死亡…危険なウイルスの詳細
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国で2000例超・754人死亡という同国史上最速のエボラアウトブレイクが進行中であり、IHR基準・WPRO基準ともに複数該当するためフルRRAへ進むべきシグナルと判断。
triage.notes: 記事は接触者追跡率が67%未満であることや、WHOがサーベイランス強化・検査能力向上・迅速対応チームの必要性を指摘している点を強調しており、アウトブレイクの制御に課題があることを示唆している。渡航制限は推奨されていない点は特記事項。

article.articleHeadline: 刚果埃博拉疫情：2千确诊754死 医护再罢工
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo Ebola outbreak: 2,000 confirmed cases, 754 deaths; healthcare workers strike again.
article.articleSummary: Congo Ebola outbreak driven by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths, with 753 patients still isolated or hospitalized and 366 recovered. Active since May 15, the outbreak marks the fastest-spreading wave yet, as transmission chains remain unknown for at least 80% of new cases and officials have yet to identify the index case. Ituri Province bears the heaviest burden amid armed conflict, displacement, and mining-driven mobility that hamper contact tracing, which covers about 67% of contacts. Many deaths occur in the community without care. Resource constraints include funding shortages, attacks on health facilities, and mistrust of the public system. Healthcare workers have staged wage protests; Bunia General Hospital and a treatment center in Rwampara have strikes, with the government pledging payments within 72 hours. Over 100 health workers infected since the outbreak.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ・エボラ流行：2000人確認、754人死亡、医療従事者が再びストライキ
triage.triage_reason: 死亡者754人、感染経路不明な症例が80%を占め、武力紛争地域での拡大が続く重大な公衆衛生上の脅威であり、IHR基準複数該当かつ社会的関心も高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwandaが含まれるが、記事本文はDRC（特にIturi州）が主題であり、Rwandaでの発生は言及されていないため除外した。ブンディブギョ・エボラウイルスによる大規模流行で、医療従事者への感染・ストライキも発生しており、対応能力に懸念がある。

article.articleHeadline: 剛果埃博拉疫情：2千確診754死 醫護再罷工
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Congo Ebola outbreak: 2,000 confirmed cases, 754 deaths; healthcare workers strike again.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, caused by Bundibugyo virus, as of July 15, 2026 reports 2,011 confirmed cases and 754 deaths, with 753 still isolated or hospitalized and 366 recovered. The surge is described as the fastest-spreading on record since it began May 15, affecting mainly Ituri Province and eastern DRC. WHO notes at least 80% of new transmission chains have unknown sources, complicating contact tracing (67% coverage). Contributing factors include ongoing armed conflict, population displacement, mining-related mobility, funding shortfalls, and attacks on medical facilities. Health workers infected exceed 100. Healthcare strikes notable: Bunia General Hospital in Ituri halted operations over unpaid wages, and a center in Rwampara saw workers protest salary arrears and bonuses, resuming after a government 72-hour payment pledge. The situation highlights resource shortages, security challenges, and community distrust hindering containment.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ(DRC)エボラ流行：確定症例2,000件、死者754人、医療従事者が再びストライキ
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ(ブンディブギョウイルス)流行が記録的速度で拡大し、死者754人・感染経路不明が8割超と深刻。医療体制崩壊・資金不足・武力紛争による人口移動も加わり、国際的拡大及び支援必要性が高い。
triage.notes: 発生地域にRwanda(Kigali Province)が含まれるが、記事本文ではルワンダでの感染事例は明記されておらず、主題はDRC(特にIturi州)のためverified_locationsから除外した。Rwamparaは地名として言及されるが所属国不明のため国際拡大の一部根拠にとどめた。

article.articleHeadline: Casos de sarampo preocupam em São Paulo e reforçam alerta sobre vacinação
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Measles cases raise concerns in São Paulo and reinforce the vaccination alert.
article.articleSummary: As of July 15, 2026, measles cases have resurfaced in São Paulo, including infections in infants, triggering renewed vaccination alerts. Measles is highly contagious and spreads through airborne droplets, with initial symptoms of high fever, cough, runny nose, red eyes, and a spreading red rash starting on the face. Complications can be serious, including pneumonia, diarrhea, ear infections, and encephalitis. Health authorities are reinforcing vaccination and surveillance, especially for babies and individuals with incomplete immunization. The measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine remains the cornerstone of prevention; during outbreaks, an additional dose may be indicated for infants aged 6–11 months. Preventive measures include frequent hand washing, avoiding contact with symptomatic people, and maintaining well-ventilated environments. Seek rapid medical care for fever with rash, report travel or contact, and follow local guidance to protect vulnerable groups.

triage.headline_ja: サンパウロで麻疹症例が懸念を呼び、ワクチン接種の警戒を強化
triage.triage_reason: サンパウロで乳児を含む麻疹症例が再燃し、当局がワクチン接種と監視体制を強化している。高い伝染性と重症化リスクがあり、WPRO基準を複数満たすためフルRRAへ進める。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジル・サンパウロでの麻疹再燃に関するもので、他の対象国への言及はない。

article.articleHeadline: DRC: more than 2,011 cumulative confirmed cases of Ebola across the three provinces - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 2,011 cumulative confirmed cases across Ituri, Nord-Kivu, and Sud-Kivu, per an epidemiological update (13 July; published 15 July 2026). There have been 754 deaths (case fatality rate 37.5%), with 753 patients in isolation or hospitalization and 366 recoveries; estimated 42 health zones across five affected provinces report a 67.4% contact-tracing rate. Haut-Uele is not included in the main report, though INRB records 14 confirmed Haut-Uele cases (June 22–July 13) including 13 deaths and 1 survivor, plus 2 suspected hospitalisations, 127 contacts traced, 14 surveys, and 5 samples awaiting dispatch. Response coordination is strengthened in Bunia and Kisangani; WHO and national teams operate in Beni (Nord-Kivu). Ituri has 25 of 36 health zones affected; Nord-Kivu 11 zones (Beni, Butembo, Goma, Kaluguta, Katwa, Kyondo, Oicha, Masereka, Bihovi, Mabalako, Musienene); Sud-Kivu: Miti-Murhesa.

triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱がDRC複数州で2,011例・754人死亡（CFR37.5%）に達しており、深刻な公衆衛生上の影響と国際的拡大リスクが認められるためフルリスク評価に進むべきシグナルと判断する。

article.articleHeadline: Pemprov Sulut Fokus Kembalikan Harapan Peternak Babi yang Terdampak ASF: Datangkan Bibit Denmark
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: North Sulawesi Provincial Government Focuses on Restoring the Hope of Pig Farmers Affected by African Swine Fever: Bring in Danish Breeding Stock.
article.articleSummary: On July 15, 2026, North Sulawesi Province, Indonesia, intensified efforts to restore its pig-farming sector hit by African Swine Fever (ASF). Deputy Governor Victor Mailangkay, representing Governor Yulius Selvanus Komaling, announced rapid government action through participation in the Indonesia–Denmark Swine Genetics Partnership in Jakarta, aiming to rehabilitate livelihoods as well as production. The initiative seeks to import Danish breeding stock, adopt superior livestock genetics, and tighten biosafety standards to raise quality and global competitiveness of Sulawesi Utara’s pig industry. The administration underlined that recovery is about restoring farmers’ hope and welfare, not only production figures. Sulawesi Utara is positioned as a potential national pig hub, with strong collaboration among government, industry players, and farmers as essential for a resilient, sustainable sector beyond ASF challenges.

triage.headline_ja: 北スラウェシ州政府、ASFの影響を受けた養豚農家の希望回復に注力：デンマークの種豚を導入

triage.notes: ASFは動物疾病でヒトに感染しないため、公衆衛生上のシグナルとしての重要性は低い。記事は養豚産業復興策に関する内容。

article.articleHeadline: %80 من إصابات "إيبولا" الجديدة مجهولة المصدر
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 80% of new Ebola cases are of unknown origin.
article.articleSummary: 80% of new Ebola infections in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo arise from transmission chains of unknown origin, signaling faster spread than health authorities’ ability to trace contacts. Government data show confirmed Ebola cases rising to 2,011, with 754 deaths. A total of 54 new infections were recorded last Monday across three provinces, including Ituri and North Kivu, as the outbreak linked to the Bundibugyo strain continues since May 15. The eastern DRC outbreak persists despite intensified response efforts, with the high share of cases from undetected chains underscoring surveillance and containment challenges. The World Health Organization continues to monitor and coordinate response efforts.

Leptospirosis cases climbed to 157 due to stagnant, contaminated water following downpours. The municipal health department has issued preventive guidelines to curb leptospira transmission. A June–July 'Special Construction Drive' tested 54,763 construction workers, uncovering 37 malaria cases. Ongoing counts include chikungunya 31, COVID-19 71, and swine flu 71. Residents are urged to take precautions, maintain hygiene, avoid standing water, and seek medical care promptly for fever and related symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Ituri : les prestataires de la riposte à Ebola annoncent la reprise des activités - ACP
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ituri: the Ebola response providers announce the resumption of activities - ACP
article.articleSummary: In Ituri, Ebola virus disease response teams in Bunia and Rwampara resumed activities after assurances from the military governor. Dr. Isaac Mungenyi, head of the Ebola Treatment Center (ETC) in Rwampara, said teams were reassured that payment arrears would be regularized and that all response pillars are valued. The dispute centered on 45 days of unpaid work and pay disparities: while some pillars were paid, communication, laboratory, and psychosocial care were left unpaid, fueling discouragement. About 148 care agents perform patient care, and nearly 90% of responders in Bunia and Rwampara were affected by delays. The delays were attributed to irregular beneficiary lists and duplicate entries. The governor pledged personal action to regularize payments, with the provincial health division coordinating. Following the meeting, the strike was suspended and teams were urged to resume patient care calmly while the issue is resolved.

article.articleHeadline: Wabah Ebola RD Kongo Tembus 2.000 Kasus, Tewaskan 754 Korban : Okezone News
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola Outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo Surpasses 2,000 Cases, Killing 754 People
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-16, Ebola virus disease cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have reached 2,011 confirmed infections with 754 deaths, government data show. The outbreak, centered in Bunia, is caused by Bundibugyo virus, a rare ebolavirus strain, and is described by Médecins Sans Frontières as the third-largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record. Transmission occurs through direct contact with blood or body fluids of infected people or animals, with typical symptoms including high fever, vomiting, and internal and external bleeding. The absence of an approved vaccine or treatment for Bundibugyo complicates response efforts, unlike outbreaks involving Zaire ebolavirus. Healthcare workers have faced added obstacles, including strikes at Bunia General Hospital over unpaid wages, hindering containment and care. MSF is urging an immediate scale-up of containment and patient care measures to address the ongoing outbreak.

article.articleHeadline: Brote de ébola en República Democrática del Congo se expande
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is expanding.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) caused by the Bundibugyo strain is expanding. As of July 11, about 2,000 cases and over 700 deaths have been reported across five provinces, making it the third-largest Ebola outbreak on record. Most new infections arise from unknown transmission chains, and roughly 80% of newly confirmed cases are not on contact-tracing lists, complicating containment. About 95% of transmission remains in Ituri, though the virus has recently reached Haut-Uele and Tshopo. In the past month, the outbreak showed its fastest growth since onset, with more than 80 new confirmed cases in 24 hours. Many deaths occurred in communities without access to healthcare; the true burden could be two to four times higher than reported. There is no approved treatment for Bundibugyo; several experimental therapies are under evaluation. Emphasis on early detection, rapid care, and community engagement—plus protection for health workers and transparent dialogue before opening centers—is urged.

article.articleHeadline: Pemkab Gorontalo Utara meluncurkan Desa Siaga Aktif TBC dan KTR
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: North Gorontalo Regency Government launches Active TB and KTR Alert Village
article.articleSummary: North Gorontalo Regency government launched Active Tuberculosis (TB) Village and Smokefree Area Task Force (Satgas Kawasan Tanpa Rokok) in Sumalata, western Gorontalo Utara, Gorontalo Province, as of 16 July 2026. The program strengthens community health by empowering villages to actively identify TB cases, ensure patients complete treatment, and reduce transmission as part of national TB elimination efforts. Irwan Abudi Usman, speaking for Regent Thariq Modanggu, announced the launch at Sabuto Hall, with attendance from the Gorontalo Utara Health Office and local officials. The Smokefree Zone Task Force aims to protect the public’s right to clean air and educate on implementing smokefree environments in health facilities, schools, places of worship, offices, and public spaces, especially safeguarding children, pregnant women, and other vulnerable groups. The initiative emphasizes joint community responsibility across districts, villages, health workers, security, and residents to sustain TB control and smokefree culture.

article.articleHeadline: Kasus DBD di Sumsel tembus 2.149 hingga Juli 2026, Kota Palembang jadi yang tertinggi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dengue fever cases in South Sumatra reach 2,149 as of July 2026, Palembang City tops the list.
article.articleSummary: 2,149 dengue fever (DBD) cases were recorded across 17 districts/cities in South Sumatra as of 14 July 2026, with 15 deaths. Palembang City accounted for the most cases (619), followed by Muara Enim (440), Ogan Ilir (185), Lubuk Linggau (139), Banyuasin (129), Lahat (128), and OKU Timur (118). Other districts reported lower counts, including Musi Banyuasin (89), OKI (67), Musi Rawas Utara (66), PALI (60), Musi Rawas (58), Prabumulih (21), OKU (16), Pagar Alam (7), Empat Lawang (4), and OKU Selatan (3). Dengue deaths were recorded in Lahat (4) and Lubuk Linggau (2), with one death in Musi Banyuasin, Banyuasin, Ogan Ilir, Palembang, PALI, and Musi Rawas Utara; others had none. El Niño may raise mosquito vectors later in 2026, risking higher cases October–December. Prevention focuses on PSN 3M Plus, larviciding/insecticiding, strengthened clinical care, and public education.

The policy, disclosed by the U.S. Department of State and reported by Reuters, aims to prevent importation of the Ebola virus amid the ongoing Congo outbreak. The report provides no specific case counts or fatalities, nor details on the duration of the restriction.

article.articleHeadline: Evaluation of two inactivated vaccines against Campylobacter fetus in an experimental bovine model: immunological survey and genital clearance in heifers - Brazilian Journal of Microbiology
article.articleSummary: Campylobacter fetus subsp. venerealis (Cfv) causes bovine genital Campylobacteriosis, a venereal disease contributing to reproductive losses in natural-service herds. In Brazil, 44 heifers were allocated to four groups: G1 vaccine A, G2 vaccine B, G3 infected with placebo, G4 negative control. After intravaginal challenge with Cfv, animals were followed for 105 days. Culture of vaginal-cervical mucus showed lower positivity in vaccinated groups (G1 61.81%, G2 45.45%) versus G3 87.27% (p<0.05). Local IgA and systemic IgG responses were detected by ELISA in all challenged groups, with earlier increases in G1/G2. Agglutinating antibodies were observed post-vaccination, strongest in G2 (p=0.0316). qPCR indicated a lower bacterial load in vaccinated cattle during sampling. Conclusion: vaccines yielded significantly earlier clearance of Cfv from the reproductive tract, associated with elevated early humoral responses; vaccines merit field evaluation to assess reproductive performance.

article.articleHeadline: Goiás registra quase 6 mil casos de SRAG em 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Goiás records nearly 6,000 cases of Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome in 2026.
article.articleSummary: In Goiás, Brazil, the State Health Secretariat reports almost 6,000 Severe Acute Respiratory Syndromes (SRAG) cases in 2026, reflecting high circulation of respiratory viruses such as Influenza and Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). Surveillance indicates ongoing SRAG activity, with children under five, the elderly, pregnant women, and people with chronic diseases most at risk for complications. Authorities stress influenza vaccination and preventive measures—frequent handwashing, covering the nose and mouth when coughing or sneezing, well-ventilated spaces, and avoiding close contact with symptomatic individuals. Patients with warning signs (shortness of breath, persistent fever, or reduced oxygenation) should seek immediate medical evaluation. The government continues epidemiological monitoring and aims to expand vaccination coverage to reduce hospitalizations from severe respiratory diseases.

article.articleHeadline: Julho Amarelo alerta para os diversos casos de hepatite
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Yellow July raises awareness about the various cases of hepatitis.
article.articleSummary: Paraná, Brazil marks Yellow July to raise awareness of viral hepatitis. From 2019–2025, Paraná recorded 7,288 hepatitis B, 5,069 hepatitis C, and 846 hepatitis A cases, with 608 related deaths. Between 2014–2024, mortality fell 75.7% for hepatitis C and 21.6% for hepatitis B, linked to expanded diagnosis and treatment access. Nationwide, Brazil reports 826,292 confirmed viral hepatitis cases from 2000–2024; hepatitis C accounts for 41.5%, hepatitis B 36.6%, and hepatitis A 21.2%. The South region accounts for 30.9% of hepatitis B and 27% of hepatitis C cases, behind the Southeast overall. Early diagnosis is emphasized, using serology (HBsAg, Anti-HBs, Anti-HBc, Anti-HCV) and molecular tests (HBV-DNA, HCV-RNA) plus liver enzymes AST, ALT, and GGT to guide treatment. Vaccination prevents hepatitis A and B (free via SUS); there is no vaccine for hepatitis C. Prevention includes safe practices, treated water, sanitation, and biosafety in procedures.

article.articleHeadline: Kasus Flu Singapura di Sumsel tembus 628, Palembang tertinggi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Singapore flu cases in South Sumatra reach 628, with Palembang the highest.
article.articleSummary: Singapore flu, or Hand, Foot and Mouth Disease (HFMD), has reached 628 cases in South Sumatra up to June 2026, with Palembang the hotspot at 118 cases. Other districts include Penukal Abab Lematang Ilir 82; Musi Banyuasin 78; Prabumulih 78; Muara Enim 65; Lahat 62; Lubuklinggau 54; Empat Lawang, Ogan Komering Ulu Timur, and Musi Rawas Utara each with 3 cases. The health office notes a clear uptick beginning in April, with tens of new weekly cases through June, reflecting HFMD’s seasonal pattern around transitions between rainy and dry seasons. The disease primarily affects children under five to seven but can infect adults with poor hygiene. Symptoms: fever, mouth ulcers, and a rash around the mouth, on hands, feet, or buttocks, plus sore throat; incubation is about 3–6 days. Severe signs—lethargy, seizures, shortness of breath, or cold extremities—require prompt hospital care.

article.articleHeadline: 6月新增新冠确诊7.9万例，其中重症130例，专家：多为轻症，不必恐慌
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In June, 79,000 new confirmed COVID-19 cases, including 130 severe cases; experts say most are mild and there is no need to panic.
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 in China: In June 2026, the country reported 79,000 new confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections nationwide (June 1–30), including 130 severe cases and 1 death with underlying conditions. Local Genomic surveillance from 31 provinces and Xinjiang = 3,741 sequences, all Omicron variants. Sentinel surveillance (late June–early July) shows COVID-19 positivity at 9.6% among influenza-like illness respiratory samples, ranking second after influenza (11.6%). Beijing You’an Hospital’s Li Tongzeng notes cases rose as population immunity waned; SARS-CoV-2 lacks a fixed season, with summer indoor ventilation practices contributing to spread. Most infections are mild, presenting upper-respiratory symptoms (low fever, sore throat, cough, nasal symptoms; some diarrhea); pneumonia and severe disease are less common. High-risk groups (elderly, chronic diseases, immunocompromised) should seek early care and antiviral treatment if symptoms arise. Other circulating pathogens include influenza (mostly type B in the south), rhinovirus, and enterovirus; and public health guidance emphasizes masking in clinics and crowded settings, hand hygiene, and ventilation.

triage.headline_ja: 6月新規新型コロナ確診7.9万例、うち重症130例、専門家「大半は軽症、パニックの必要なし」
triage.triage_reason: COVID-19の季節的な感染者増加であり、専門家も軽症が大半でパニック不要と説明。異常性・国際的拡大リスク・渡航貿易制限のいずれも認められず、通常のサーベイランス報告の範囲内。
triage.notes: 既知のOmicron株による季節的増加であり、変異株の異常性や重症度上昇の兆候はない。中国国内の通常のサーベイランス報告。

article.articleHeadline: US says it is blocking Americans in DR Congo from immediate travel home, citing Ebola
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-07-16, the United States has imposed travel restrictions tied to an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). American citizens and nationals who have been in the DRC within the past 21 days are prohibited from entering the United States via commercial air travel. The policy, announced by the State Department, aims to curb potential importation of Ebola during the outbreak in the DRC. The report does not provide case or death counts. The measure underscores heightened concern over travel from Ebola-affected regions and applies to commercial aviation routes.

triage.headline_ja: 米国、エボラを理由にコンゴ民主共和国滞在の米国人の即時帰国便を制限していると発表
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の発生を受けて米国が渡航制限を課しており、IHR基準の複数（渡航制限、国際的拡大リスク、深刻な公衆衛生影響）に該当するためフルRRAへ進めるべき。
triage.notes: 記事は米国の渡航制限措置に焦点を当てており、DRCでのエボラ発生自体の症例数・死亡数は記載されていない。米国は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。続報でDRC国内の感染状況の詳細確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: A Deadly Ebola-Like Virus Is Spreading. Are We Ready?
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus, a filovirus closely related to Ebola, is driving a deadly outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, with 695 confirmed cases and 138 deaths as of June 11, according to the WHO. The outbreak gained formal recognition after the death of a nurse. Bundibugyo causes severe hemorrhagic fever, marked by inflammation, vascular damage, bleeding, and multi-organ failure. Transmission occurs via direct contact with infected bodily fluids, placing health workers at high risk, especially in hospitals. Diagnosis is difficult because early symptoms resemble malaria and typhoid; laboratory confirmation is essential. In the DRC, limited local testing requires samples to travel to national reference labs, delaying confirmation and hindering isolation and contact tracing. Sullivan argues preparedness must extend beyond vaccines to include operational readiness for multinational outbreak response, noting there is no Bundibugyo-specific vaccine or therapy; vaccines for other filoviruses may offer protection but are not substitutes.

triage.headline_ja: 致死性のエボラ様ウイルスが拡大中。我々に備えはあるか？
triage.triage_reason: コンゴ民主共和国・ウガンダでブンディブギョウイルス（エボラ近縁のフィロウイルス）による出血熱アウトブレイクが発生し、695症例・138死亡（致死率約20%）と深刻。医療従事者への感染、診断遅延、特異的ワクチン・治療薬の欠如など複数のIHR基準に該当する。
triage.notes: ウガンダも発生地域として挙げられているが、対象国リストに含まれないためverified_locationsには含めない。DRCでは検査能力の制約により診断・隔離・接触者追跡が遅延している点が特筆される。
